feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector roles: the positioning is clear, experience progression is logical, and the content shows broad ownership across strategy, platforms, analytics, and multimedia. Impact is solid but could be sharper with more outcome-focused metrics, and the document feels slightly repetitive across skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative with strong career progression at NACo, culminating in director-level ownership and current consulting work.  
- Good credibility through concrete scope indicators: 10,000+ page site, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, named tools/platforms, and public-sector specialization.  
- Writing is generally polished, professional, and consistent in tone; no obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more results, not just responsibilities: include measurable outcomes such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, campaign performance, adoption rates, or cost savings.  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; punctuation/hyphenation varies slightly (“front-end,” “organization-wide,” “member-facing” are consistent, but bullet formatting in work entries/footer is dense and could be cleaner).
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads broad and repeats themes covered in Core Competencies and Work Experience. It would be stronger with one or two concrete scale signals and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic “building the platforms” language with sharper action verbs and outcomes, e.g. “leading modernization of enterprise web, analytics, and editorial systems.”
- Add a scale cue from recent experience to increase impact, such as “10,000+ page website,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Tighten the second sentence by grouping related capabilities and reducing list-like phrasing.
- Consider revised version: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web platforms, governance models, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Leads website transformation, analytics ecosystems, editorial workflows, and multimedia programs—including AI-enabled search and content experiences—for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; “AI-enabled search and content experiences” is more specific.
- The long capability list duplicates later skills sections; keep the intro more positioning-focused.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize distinctive leadership-level capabilities rather than repeating broad phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and sharpen wording: “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization.”
- Prioritize the most differentiating strengths first: web modernization, governance/editorial systems, analytics, AI search, automation/integrations.
- Consider a tighter version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Replace “content experiences” with “content discovery” or “user experiences” for more specificity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” and “Multi-channel communications operations” substantially repeat the header and Topline Skills.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” is already well covered in Topline Skills and multiple roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it currently repeats several themes already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense for a footer. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope where possible would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use stronger, outcome-oriented verbs and simplify lists: e.g., “Created an AI-powered legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, and bill-level chat.”
- Standardize style across entries: use either all “Built/Developed/Launched” phrasing or all noun-led project summaries.
- If available, add one concrete result, audience, or scale marker to 1–2 projects to increase specificity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with NACo experience bullets; reframe as “selected examples” rather than restating responsibilities.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item; consider leading with it or another less-redundant project.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a services list rather than a high-impact consulting entry. Tighten it around strategic outcomes and avoid repeating NACo platform/governance themes already covered in prior roles and Recent Projects.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + value: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and web modernization as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 outcome-led bullets; e.g., “Built cross-channel workflows, analytics and governance systems to improve coordination across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Separate strategic from technical work: one bullet for Drupal campaign/microsite delivery, one for CMS/front-end troubleshooting, one for AI search leadership.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, toolkit downloads, search accuracy gains, publishing time reduced, stakeholder teams served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, and enterprise web improvement” overlaps heavily with the Director of Digital Media entry; emphasize consultant-level advisory/remediation work instead.
- Drupal microsites and AI search are already echoed in Recent Projects, so keep this item higher-level and outcome-focused.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia production and multi-channel communications operations.”
- Combine oversight bullets and foreground the biggest win: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more results-oriented; add performance metrics if available (email growth, engagement, social growth, video output, cost savings, turnaround time).
- Tighten remaining bullets to impact language: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio…” / “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery reporting…” / “Established governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version higher-level and outcome-focused.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older NACo roles unless this bullet stresses the studio build and expanded organizational capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the roles before and after it. Make it more specific to what changed under your leadership at this level, with sharper outcomes and less generic “helped” language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy delivery.”
- Replace weak verbs like “helped scale,” “helped improve,” and “strengthened” with direct action verbs: managed, launched, built, standardized, coordinated.
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets into one stronger line: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and content delivery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and the footer project; clarify this role as scaling/formalizing the series rather than originating it.
- “Digital communications operations across web, email, social and video” is very close to the 2022–2024 entry; keep this version focused on execution and process-building, not overall leadership.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should sharpen the candidate’s senior-level positioning and reflect the most recent enterprise/public-sector leadership work.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with tighter, higher-signal wording tied to recent scope:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social, and video
- Audience-centered content strategy and advocacy storytelling
- Consider swapping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” for “Mission-driven stakeholder communications” if targeting broader roles.
- Keep wording parallel and noun-based; avoid vague terms like “planning” when “strategy” or “operations” is stronger.
- If space allows, add one scale cue in the section title or nearby summary instead of here (e.g., enterprise web modernization, 10,000+ pages, 50+ publishers).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” also repeats experience bullets; tighten to avoid saying the same thing three times.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill mix, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes over listing every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • Web modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Drop lower-priority or older-signal items unless they are current differentiators; keep Drupal prominent given the recent 10,000+ page migration and current consulting work.
- Replace “jQuery” with “front-end implementation” or remove it; it reads dated and adds little at topline level.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites” to better connect skills to impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, API integrations, and Airtable already appear in Technical + IT; avoid repeating the same inventory here.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies, so keep wording distinct or shorten it to “AI-enabled search.”

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. Make it more outcome-oriented and slightly more strategic.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, BigQuery, Looker Studio and Power BI reporting”
- Replace generic items with impact language: “KPI framework design and executive dashboarding” instead of “KPI design” and “Leadership reporting”
- Tighten final item to “SEO, content performance and conversion analysis” if accurate
- Consider ordering by strategic value, not tools: “Analytics strategy • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding • GA4/BigQuery/Power BI/Looker Studio • UX insight via Microsoft Clarity • SEO and performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills more strategic and reserve full tool inventory for Technical + IT.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and multiple NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and operational scope rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tools/tasks to leadership-level capabilities: “Broadcast-quality studio production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and control-room workflows • Video editing and post-production”
- If space allows, add scale or context tied to recent work: “Built and operated an in-house studio supporting advocacy programming, recurring video content, and hybrid events.”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more senior phrase like “End-to-end video production” or “Studio and field video production.”
- Consider dropping “virtual” if “hybrid event delivery” already covers it; “livestream” + “hybrid” is more specific.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording.
- “Studio operations” and “PTZ camera systems” are supported by the Director of Digital Media bullet about building the in-house studio, so keep this skills line concise.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either add context/seniority or be tightened to avoid repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize strongest, most recent platforms first: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of just names: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing and consistency with the rest of the CV.
- If no qualifiers can be added, shorten the list by dropping the least material platform to keep focus on recent impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep the fuller version in one place and make this one shorter or more outcome-oriented.
- Drupal already appears repeatedly in recent experience, so avoid over-indexing on it without adding new context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should emphasize implementation tools not already covered elsewhere and use cleaner, more current phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation**
- Tighten and modernize the list: **HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions**
- Consider dropping **jQuery** unless it is still actively used in recent work; if kept, place it last to signal legacy familiarity rather than core capability.
- If space allows, add specificity tied to recent work: **JavaScript for Drupal front-end enhancements • serverless scripting with Cloudflare Workers • CI/CD automation with GitHub Actions**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations** already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact same phrasing in both places.
- **Workflow automation** is covered elsewhere, so keep this item focused on coding/implementation tools rather than broader systems language.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item mixes true automation platforms with general collaboration/project tools, which weakens the “systems” signal. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” already emphasized elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function and lead with actual automation tools: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira Automations”
- Move general collaboration tools to a separate item or relabel this entry to: “Automation, Project & Collaboration Systems”
- If accurate, add higher-signal phrasing tied to use: “Airtable databases/interfaces • Power Automate flows • Zapier integrations • Jira/Asana workflow management”
- Consider trimming lower-value tools unless used heavily in recent roles; prioritize platforms tied to current consulting and director-level systems work

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same language here
- Slack, Teams, and Trello read as generic unless they support a stronger systems/operations narrative

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a generic tool list and misses the scale/complexity implied elsewhere in the CV. It should signal enterprise email operations and audience engagement without repeating newsletter management already covered in work experience.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten/standardize platform names: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show level: **Enterprise campaign automation, newsletter operations, and member communications**
- Keep it platform-focused; let the work experience carry audience size and program ownership

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding “email newsletters,” “tens of thousands,” or channel leadership language here; that is already covered in the Director/Associate Director roles.
- “Engagement” may overlap with broader “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies; consider “Member Engagement Platforms” only if that reflects actual use.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and the Director role. Make it more specific to methods/tools and trim broad terms.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • KPI design • SEO/performance analysis • Experimentation (A/B testing)**
- Replace vague nouns like **Dashboarding** with stronger capability language such as **KPI design**, **reporting**, or **performance analysis**.
- If space allows, group by function for readability: **Analytics:** GA4, Clarity, BigQuery | **Reporting:** Looker Studio, Power BI | **Optimization:** SEO, A/B testing.
- Only keep items you can support with outcomes elsewhere (e.g., analytics infrastructure expansion, reporting improvements).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly identical to **Topline Skills [3] Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; differentiate this section as tool-focused and keep the topline section leadership/outcomes-focused.
- “Dashboarding” repeats the reporting idea already implied by Looker Studio and Power BI.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, with concrete outputs rather than team/operations language that is covered more strongly in 2018–2024 roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career build work: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function.”
- Add specific outputs and scope: website refresh support, livestream production, weekly video series, and channel support across web/email/social/multimedia.
- Replace soft phrasing like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows” with actions and results; add metrics if available (e.g., number of livestreams, videos produced, audience growth, email volume).
- Tighten to one sentence or two concise bullets, e.g.: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates. Coordinated day-to-day publishing across web, email, social and multimedia, while informally guiding a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthening workflows” and cross-channel operations repeat points made more credibly in the 2018–2024 NACo entries.
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; distinguish this as launch/early production support if accurate.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy communications.”
- Add a second sentence focused on the standout deliverable: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with a more specific outcome or channel, if available (e.g., web features, audio content, program collateral).
- If possible, add scope: number of episodes launched, audiences served, or programs/policy areas supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media roles; keep this item centered on research/program support and the first podcast launch.
- Avoid claiming broad digital leadership here, since stronger, more recent entries already cover that progression.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful supporting skills, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with stronger, more recent experience bullets and the “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” skills section. Tighten it to emphasize tools only, not capabilities already proven elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
